slides.title: The approval queue
slides.gate: Ready for your permission to start
slides.sub: Review this plan before giving permission.
slides.see: 1. Existing search and spec groups lead into the selected item. The selected workflow phase supplies the current gate and next action.
slides.act: 2. Select an item, inspect its plan, then use its eligible owner action. Keep search and the existing group order.
slides.why: 3. A quiet sidebar and one content heading replace repeated cards and competing stage badges. Revision metadata moves into existing details.
slides.feedback: 4. Selection gains a subtle blue fill. Current-gate text outranks a stale deliverable label. Keyboard focus stays visible.
slides.boundary: List labels use existing list workflow data. No bulk approval, added inbox or new status field.

slides.title: The brief and incomplete plan
slides.gate: The plan is still being prepared
slides.sub: Task definitions are incomplete. Owner approval is not available yet.
slides.see: 1. The existing owner panel explains the current wait. The brief is expanded and other document disclosures remain available.
slides.act: 2. Read the brief or open the existing plan document. Show no approval action while the workflow is in the plan phase.
slides.why: 3. Scope appears before technical detail. Quiet document disclosures avoid multiple tall cards and nested visual frames.
slides.feedback: 4. Expanding a document retains its place and focus. Missing artifacts have explicit text rather than an empty rectangle.
slides.boundary: Display the existing workflow reasons. Do not create a request-plan action or let the owner edit task definitions here.

slides.title: Spec questions and an unknown answer
slides.gate: An answer is still needed
slides.sub: Q-2 remains unresolved. Recording an unknown answer keeps this gate open.
slides.see: 1. The first unresolved question sits above supporting requirements. The saved unknown state remains explicit beside the question.
slides.act: 2. Type an answer and choose Answer. Keep I don’t know as a quieter existing secondary action.
slides.why: 3. The user handles one visible question before reading supporting material. Completed answers remain in existing disclosures below.
slides.feedback: 4. On a successful response, announce Answer recorded and focus the next unresolved question. On failure, retain the typed answer.
slides.boundary: The count comes from loaded clarifications. Unknown does not count as resolved. No automatic approval or hidden answer submission.

slides.title: Spec approval after answers
slides.gate: The spec is ready for your approval
slides.sub: All registered spec questions are resolved. Review the recorded answers.
slides.see: 1. The current gate, answer summary and existing spec disclosure share one reading column.
slides.act: 2. Approve this spec arms the existing confirmation. A second deliberate click records the approval with the current owner claim.
slides.why: 3. Answers stay visible near the approval action. The design removes unrelated instructions instead of asking users to infer readiness.
slides.feedback: 4. First click changes the same button to Confirm spec approval and explains the recorded act inline. Busy state prevents duplicate submissions.
slides.boundary: Keep the current two-click library approval. Empty phase-question lists skip this ceremony. Approval still grants no Start permission.

slides.title: Design decision acceptance
slides.gate: A design decision needs your review
slides.sub: D-2 is proposed. Read its rationale before accepting it.
slides.see: 1. The current proposed decision and its because text appear before supporting design parts. Accepted decisions stay available below.
slides.act: 2. Accept D-2 records only this decision. Each remaining proposal still needs its own existing acceptance action.
slides.why: 3. One expanded proposal has the strongest action. Secondary proposals and design diagrams use existing content disclosures.
slides.feedback: 4. A saved acceptance changes the written status and moves focus to the next proposal. Success depends on the returned workflow state.
slides.boundary: No Accept all, decision editing or automatic Start. Preserve individual decision IDs, rejection reasons and authority.

slides.title: A decision rejection
slides.gate: A design decision needs your review
slides.sub: D-2 is still proposed. A rejection reason is required.
slides.see: 1. The existing Reject disclosure is open beneath the same decision. The rationale remains visible above the reason field.
slides.act: 2. Enter the reason and choose Reject D-2. Acceptance stays secondary while this disclosure has focus.
slides.why: 3. The less common action reveals its required field only when needed. The user keeps the original decision in view.
slides.feedback: 4. An empty reason produces an inline field error and focused guidance. A saved rejection displays Declined and the returned blocking reason.
slides.boundary: Rejection uses the existing owner action. Declined required choices still block dependent work. No undo or reopen control is invented.

slides.title: The task plan and permission to start
slides.gate: The plan is ready to start
slides.sub: Decisions are accepted. Review the full task sequence and its checks.
slides.see: 1. Task titles, dependencies and declared checks remain accessible. The existing Start button stays beside a short permission explanation.
slides.act: 2. Start implementation grants permission for this exact plan. Keep the action in the existing owner panel, sticky within its content column.
slides.why: 3. A stable action position avoids a long trip back to the top after reading tasks. Technical trace links expand only on demand.
slides.feedback: 4. Show Saving permission while the existing request is pending. After success, display Permission recorded and the returned phase.
slides.boundary: Use can_start and the existing revision guard. The browser records permission and does not wake an idle agent. No instant-running claim.

slides.title: Implementation in progress
slides.gate: Implementation is in progress
slides.sub: Permission is recorded for this plan. Two of four tasks are complete.
slides.see: 1. Existing task statuses lead each row. The current task stays expanded with its declared check. Completed evidence sits in a disclosure.
slides.act: 2. Inspect the current task or use the existing refresh trigger when state may have changed. There is no owner approval to repeat here.
slides.why: 3. Removing prior approval instructions makes progress immediately legible. Task counts come directly from the loaded tasks.
slides.feedback: 4. Completed tasks show a checkmark and the word Done. State refreshes through existing interaction and focus behavior, without invented live telemetry.
slides.boundary: Display approved execution state, not agent presence. No Run, pause, retry or new polling service. Keep independent review as the next gate.

slides.title: A blocked task
slides.gate: Implementation needs attention
slides.sub: The current task cannot continue. Inspect the recorded reason and evidence.
slides.see: 1. The blocked task moves above completed evidence. Existing reasons and any failed command result appear next to its status.
slides.act: 2. Read the blocker, inspect its evidence and refresh when the agent has repaired the issue. Do not offer a browser bypass.
slides.why: 3. The specific blocking reason replaces a generic warning panel. Only the affected task expands by default.
slides.feedback: 4. Amber pairs with the word Blocked. A failed command retains its actual exit code. Refresh changes the display only after a new response.
slides.boundary: Source drift and a changed plan remain distinct. A changed plan uses the existing Start gate again. No repin, retry-task or force-approve UI.

slides.title: Independent review pending
slides.gate: Independent review is pending
slides.sub: Task checks passed. The independent reviewer still needs to assess this plan and evidence.
slides.see: 1. The existing review empty state sits below the current gate. The phase inspector shows Finish as a later step.
slides.act: 2. Inspect available evidence. No Finish control appears until the existing workflow declares the pack eligible.
slides.why: 3. The screen explains exactly who must act next. Completion and owner attention no longer compete with review waiting.
slides.feedback: 4. Existing refresh behavior reveals the returned review result. A passing task check never animates into a passing PACK review.
slides.boundary: No Request review button, reviewer assignment or live activity indicator. Keep can_close authoritative.

slides.title: The reviewed pack is ready to finish
slides.gate: The spec is ready for you to finish
slides.sub: Task checks and the current independent review passed.
slides.see: 1. The current PACK verdict leads the review list. Reviewer identity and recorded evidence remain available beneath it.
slides.act: 2. Inspect the verdict, then choose Finish spec. This reveals the existing confirmation in place.
slides.why: 3. A short readiness statement and one primary action replace scattered success badges. The review remains adjacent to the final decision.
slides.feedback: 4. Show the Finish action only when can_close is true. Review filters retain access to earlier findings without obscuring the current verdict.
slides.boundary: Earlier PASS records are not current eligibility. The workflow response remains authoritative. Unresolved feedback does not become a new finish gate.

slides.title: Finish confirmation
slides.gate: Finish and freeze this spec?
slides.sub: The completed record becomes read-only. This is a separate owner action.
slides.see: 1. The existing confirmation replaces the Finish button inside the owner panel. The pack title and current review remain visible.
slides.act: 2. Yes, finish spec records completion. Keep open cancels the confirmation and restores the original action.
slides.why: 3. The consequence is plain and close to the control. No extra dialog, screen, typing challenge or approval ceremony is added.
slides.feedback: 4. Focus enters the existing confirmation. Cancellation returns focus to Finish spec. While saving, disable duplicate controls and announce progress.
slides.boundary: Keep both existing confirmation choices and the distinct close action. Never auto-finish after a PASS or a Resolve event.

slides.title: The completed spec
slides.gate: The spec is complete
slides.sub: The owner marked this record complete. Its history is frozen.
slides.see: 1. Completion replaces the action area with a concise recorded state. The same tabs and phase inspector remain available for inspection.
slides.act: 2. Read the review, task evidence or feedback history. Existing navigation provides the route back to other library items.
slides.why: 3. One completion heading communicates the outcome. Repeated green badges and inactive approval buttons add no useful information.
slides.feedback: 4. Focus lands on the completion heading after a successful response. Read-only history retains text selection and document navigation.
slides.boundary: No Reopen, duplicate item or new summary screen. Closed feedback controls stay disabled under existing rules.

slides.title: Document feedback as a draft
slides.gate: The plan is ready to start
slides.sub: Feedback is separate from owner approval. This session reviews a selected document.
slides.see: 1. Existing session, round and file controls form a compact toolbar. The selected source line appears beside the comment field.
slides.act: 2. Select the existing anchor, write the comment and Save draft comment. Submit feedback stays a separate action after the comment is saved.
slides.why: 3. A two-column source and discussion arrangement shortens eye movement. Scope and draft state stay visible near the action.
slides.feedback: 4. Selection gains a blue line highlight. The save response says Draft saved, then the same Submit feedback control gains visual priority.
slides.boundary: Keep comment and submit as separate existing requests. Local input is not a submitted batch. No combined Save and send action.

slides.title: A revised code diff and thread resolution
slides.gate: Implementation is in progress
slides.sub: A newer review round is available. Inspect the change before resolving its thread.
slides.see: 1. The existing round selector points to the newest round. Before and After remain available. The thread and agent response sit beside the source.
slides.act: 2. Inspect the revised lines, then use that thread’s Resolve button. Resolve each remaining thread independently.
slides.why: 3. The source and discussion share a visual baseline. The user sees what changed and why without moving across several stacked panels.
slides.feedback: 4. A successful response changes Unresolved to Resolved and disables its action. Original anchors and submitted batches remain accessible.
slides.boundary: Do not claim auto-delivery or agent presence. An idle agent needs a prompt. Resolve grants no approval, Start or Finish permission.

slides.title: A stale feedback anchor
slides.gate: A comment needs a new anchor
slides.sub: The source changed. The original comment remains attached to its original round.
slides.see: 1. The existing stale status labels the thread. The latest open round and new selected source line remain visible beside it.
slides.act: 2. Select the new anchor, choose Reattach to selected anchor, then Submit feedback. These remain two separate recorded actions.
slides.why: 3. Context, selection and the recovery action stay together. A stale comment does not disappear into a generic error message.
slides.feedback: 4. Announce Reattachment saved as a draft. Visual priority then moves to the existing Submit feedback control, after a successful response.
slides.boundary: Never infer or silently move an anchor. A sealed round requires an agent-published new round. Preserve View original anchor.

slides.title: A feedback revision conflict
slides.gate: Feedback changed while you were reviewing
slides.sub: Refresh before retrying. Your local draft is retained.
slides.see: 1. The existing feedback error sits next to the comment field. The selected source and retained text stay visible.
slides.act: 2. Refresh feedback, inspect the current round and retry the intended existing action. Keep the draft and the spec owner controls separate.
slides.why: 3. A specific recovery instruction replaces a broad red banner. Draft retention avoids retyping and makes the interrupted work recoverable.
slides.feedback: 4. Focus the error announcement without erasing the draft. Show a busy refresh state and update source selection deliberately.
slides.boundary: Retain the existing operation identity and revision checks. Do not automatically resend, submit a new batch or reattach after conflict.

slides.title: An owner action revision conflict
slides.gate: The spec changed before the action could be saved
slides.sub: Refresh the spec and review its current plan before trying again.
slides.see: 1. The existing owner error and Refresh control sit directly beside the owner action area. The attempted action remains understandable.
slides.act: 2. Refresh the spec, reread changed content, then deliberately repeat the eligible action if it is still appropriate.
slides.why: 3. Recovery lives at the point of interruption. The UI makes no claim that permission exists when the server refused the write.
slides.feedback: 4. Focus the error. Disable duplicate requests while refreshing. Restore an action only from the new workflow response.
slides.boundary: Never advance optimistically or auto-retry approval. Keep expected_revision, plan identity and all server eligibility rules unchanged.

slides.title: A recorded action with pending audit recovery
slides.gate: Your permission was recorded
slides.sub: The audit journal still needs recovery. The canonical owner receipt already exists.
slides.see: 1. The existing audit_pending message appears beneath the recorded permission state. Task content remains available.
slides.act: 2. Read the state and refresh after recovery. The owner does not repeat an action that already landed.
slides.why: 3. The UI distinguishes a durable receipt from a journal problem. A quiet amber message prevents a second approval prompted by uncertainty.
slides.feedback: 4. Present the actual pending-entry count only when returned. Announce the recorded action, then the outstanding recovery status.
slides.boundary: No Recover audit button or backend repair. No invented journal completion. Avoid showing Start again because an append failed.

slides.title: Approval state unavailable
slides.gate: Owner actions are unavailable
slides.sub: Refresh the spec to read its current approval state.
slides.see: 1. The existing unavailable state occupies the owner panel. Already available document content stays readable.
slides.act: 2. Use the existing Refresh control. Approval actions stay hidden until the workflow response has loaded consistently.
slides.why: 3. The message explains the interruption and offers the supported recovery path. The screen does not collapse into an empty error page.
slides.feedback: 4. Announce unavailable and refreshing states. Restore focus to the current-gate heading after a successful refresh.
slides.boundary: Do not infer can_start or can_close from cached content, task counts or an old PASS. No new error screen or endpoint.

slides.title: Feedback before a session exists
slides.gate: There is no review session yet
slides.sub: Ask your agent to open selected documents or code changes for review.
slides.see: 1. The existing feedback empty state explains why no source or thread is available. Spec navigation remains visible.
slides.act: 2. The next step is the existing agent workflow outside this browser. Refresh feedback after the agent opens the session.
slides.why: 3. Clear scope avoids offering a dead comment box. The user knows that a review session must exist before leaving feedback.
slides.feedback: 4. Keep the empty message stable while a refresh is pending. Show a session only when the existing state response supplies one.
slides.boundary: No Create session, agent chat composer or wake-agent action. The browser’s current feedback endpoints retain their existing scope.

slides.title: The existing interview room
slides.gate: Question 1 of 2
slides.sub: Choose an answer, then submit it. The dossier stays within reach.
slides.see: 1. The existing dossier, focused interview and question count retain their layout roles. Choice labels use full rows with visible selection.
slides.act: 2. Choose an existing option and Submit. Back and I don’t know remain secondary. Preserve the current keyboard behavior.
slides.why: 3. One question fills the center rather than competing with the entire spec. The selected option and submit action form one clear reading path.
slides.feedback: 4. Keep 1–9 choice hints and j/k navigation. Enter submits, Shift+Enter adds a line in free text. Successful answers advance through the existing room.
slides.boundary: This is the existing page.html room, not a new wizard. Room approval remains separate from library Start and Finish actions.

slides.title: Legacy history remains read-only
slides.gate: Historical record
slides.sub: This archived initiative is read-only and uses its original workflow.
slides.see: 1. The existing History group opens the preserved dossier. Historical labels and documents remain available without owner controls.
slides.act: 2. Inspect the record or choose another existing item in the library. Do not show gated actions for a historical entry.
slides.why: 3. A persistent read-only heading avoids disabled-button clutter and separates current workflow readiness from historical evidence.
slides.feedback: 4. Preserve search, focus and disclosure behavior. Show the source’s actual historic state without converting it into a current gate.
slides.boundary: No browser migration, adoption, editing or reopen action. Legacy active records retain their own rules and are distinct from archived history.

style: Quiet Workspace: system sans serif, white content, soft gray navigation, near-black text, one blue primary action, 44 px primary action controls, 8 px spacing rhythm and 10 px corners. Green and amber always accompany written status. Existing light/dark preference, routes and nine owner steps remain.
scope: Design artifact only. No application source or live state changed.
